f.title: Establish research questions in advance for post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities
f.statement: When conducting post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities, specific issues (research questions) should be established in advance, whatever the study method, in order to obtain scientific evidence leading to effective safety measures.
f.clause: 2. Planning and conducting of a study using the medical information databases

f.title: Consider a medical information database study when it is expected to be appropriate and expeditious
f.statement: Based on its purpose, a study using medical information databases should be considered when it is expected to be appropriate with expedition. The source gives examples where it may be appropriate, including: exploring the frequency, trend or related factors in a specific population of an event of concern found in ADR reports; studying actual prescription status to plan proper-use information; and where it is inappropriate for the MAH and others to collect data from medical institutions themselves given the number of cases and study period required.
f.clause: 2. Planning and conducting of a study using the medical information databases (quote ends at a page break)
f.applicability: English translation by PMDA (reference only; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSEHB/PED Notification No. 0609-8 and PSEHB/SD Notification No. 0609-4. Applies mainly to post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities for new drugs using medical information databases.

rows.quote: Based on its purpose, the implementation of the study using the medical information databases should be considered, when the study is expected to be appropriate with expedition. For example, a study using the medical information databases may be appropriate in the following cases: ・ When an event of concern is found in the information of adverse drug reaction reporting, the frequency and trend of the event, or factors related to it in a specific population are explored; ・ When the actual status of prescription is studied in order to consider the method and contents for providing information on proper use; ・ When it is considered inappropriate to conduct a study in which the marketing authorization holders and other entities collect data from medical institutions by themselves, taking into account the number of cases and study period required for evaluation;
rows.location: 2. Planning and conducting of a study using the medical information databases (quote ends at a page break)
rows.review_note: Review: statement reworded to make clear the cases are non-exhaustive examples; the quote stops at a page header, after which the source adds control-group studies of events occurring regardless of drug use and evaluation of the effect of safety measures. Double-check: examples cut at a page header (later examples not quoted); 'should be considered' is soft; below 90: PMDA English reference translation (Japanese original prevails), MAH actor inferred.

f.title: Confirm data reliability and examine database characteristics before selecting a database
f.statement: For selection of medical information databases, it should be confirmed that data reliability is ensured, and the characteristics of the database (owner, period of accumulated data, sample size and population characteristics, traceability, range of drugs and adverse events that can be studied, and procedures for obtaining data) should be sufficiently examined in advance.
f.applicability: English translation by PMDA (reference only; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSEHB/PED Notification No. 0609-8 and PSEHB/SD Notification No. 0609-4. Applies mainly to post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities for new drugs using medical information databases.

rows.quote: For selection of medical information databases, it should be confirmed that the reliability of the data is ensured, and sufficient examination should be performed in advance on the characteristics of the database such as the owner of the database, period of the accumulated data, sample size and characteristics of the population to be studied, traceability, range of drugs that can be studied, adverse events that can be studied, and procedures for obtaining data.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves both 'should' duties and the listed characteristics; below 90: PMDA English reference translation (Japanese original prevails), MAH actor inferred.

f.title: Examine data elements, study plan and statistical method in advance following the PMDA 2014 guideline
f.statement: Based on the PMDA "Guideline for the Conduct of Pharmaco-epidemiological Studies in Drug Safety Assessment with Medical Information Database" (31 Mar 2014), the characteristics of the data elements used for evaluation should be carefully examined, and the study plan and statistical method should be examined sufficiently in advance; it is important to make the plan after fully understanding the clinical significance of the data elements and how they are operated in medical practice.
f.clause: 4. Development of study plan using medical information databases, (1)
f.applicability: English translation by PMDA (reference only; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSEHB/PED Notification No. 0609-8 and PSEHB/SD Notification No. 0609-4. Applies mainly to post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities for new drugs using medical information databases.

rows.quote: (1) Based on the “Guideline for the Conduct of Pharmaco-epidemiological Studies in Drug Safety Assessment with Medical Information Database” (dated March 31, 2014, by the PMDA), the characteristics of the data elements to be used for evaluation should be carefully examined, and then the study plan and its statistical method should also be examined sufficiently in advance. In particular, it is important to make the plan after fully understanding the clinical significance of the data elements, method of operation on the data elements in medical practice, etc.
rows.location: 4. Development of study plan using medical information databases, (1)

f.title: Prevent feasibility or tentative analyses from biasing the study plan in favour of the drug
f.statement: When a feasibility study, tentative analysis or similar is conducted before developing the study plan to examine the database, study design or analysis method, sufficient attention should be paid so that the plan is not made intentionally advantageous to the drug studied.
f.clause: 4. Development of study plan using medical information databases, (2)

rows.quote: (2) When a feasibility study, tentative analysis, etc. are conducted to examine a database to be used, study design, or analysis method, etc. prior to the development of the study plan, sufficient attention should be paid lest the developed survey plan should be intentionally advantageous to the drug to be studied.

f.statement: When an existing drug is used as a control, an appropriate drug should be selected from scientific and clinical viewpoints, also based on the treatment guideline for the indication and the mechanism of action of the drug.

f.title: Evaluate database study results comprehensively before changing PV or risk minimisation activities
f.statement: When pharmacovigilance or risk minimisation activities are added, changed or terminated based on the results of a database study, the decision should be made after carefully evaluating the clinical significance of the results and comprehensively evaluating them together with other information.
f.applicability: English translation by PMDA (reference only; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSEHB/PED Notification No. 0609-8 and PSEHB/SD Notification No. 0609-4. Applies mainly to post-marketing pharmacovigilance activities for new drugs using medical information databases.
